translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna! You praise the renunciation of actions, and then You praise the Yoga of selfless action. Tell me decisively which one of these two is better and more beneficial for me.

The Blessed Lord said: Both the formal renunciation of action and the Yoga of selfless action lead to liberation. But of the two, the Yoga of selfless action is superior to the mere renunciation of action.
simple_explanation: Renunciation of action defines a state of mind free from bias. This mental clarity is verified only when tested in the field of action. An attached person chooses tools that harm his ultimate goal out of narrow favoritism. Action combined with detachment is superior.

translation: He who neither hates nor desires anything should be known as a perpetual renunciant (Nitya- sannyasi). For one who is free from dualities, O mighty-armed one, is easily liberated from all bondage.
The ignorant speak of analytical knowledge (Sankhya) and the Yoga of action as separate, but the wise do not. One who is properly established in even one of them reaps the fruits of both.
The status achieved by the practitioners of Sankhya is also reached by the practitioners of Karmayoga. He who sees Sankhya and Yoga as one sees things as they really are.
But renunciation, O mighty-armed one, is difficult to attain without the practice of Yoga. The reflective sage anchored in Yoga attains Brahman without delay.

He who is anchored in Yoga, whose mind is pure, who has mastered his lower self, whose senses are controlled, and who identifies his own self with the self of all living beings (sarva- bhuta-atma-bhutatma), is never tainted even though he performs actions.
The knower of Truth, absorbed in Yoga, should realize, "I do not perform any action independently," while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, or breathing;
While speaking, evacuating wastes, grasping, opening, or closing his eyes—convinced that "it is merely the senses interacting with their respective sense objects."
He who performs actions surrendering them to the Cosmic Order, abandoning all attachment, is untouched by sin, just as a lotus leaf remains unwetted by water.
Yogis perform actions using their body, mind, intellect, and detached senses, solely for the purpose of self-purification (Atma-shuddhaye), casting off all personal attachment.
The integrated practitioner, renouncing the fruits of action, attains everlasting peace. But the unintegrated person, driven by selfish desire and attached to rewards, is heavily bound.

Mentally surrendering all actions, the self-controlled embodied soul dwells happily in the city of nine gates (the physical body), neither working for individual ego nor causing ego-driven results. He acts as an instrument of the Divine.

The Supreme Lord does not engineer individual ego-agency, nor does He script personal actions or forge the link between action and its reward. All this is driven by the momentum of one's own natural disposition (Svabhava).
The omnipresent Lord does not take upon Himself the sin of anyone, nor does He claim anyone's virtue. True knowledge is enveloped by ignorance; therefore, creatures fall into delusion.
simple_explanation: People carry false beliefs that an incarnation will directly absorb their personal sins or that a specific formula can destroy an adversary's merit. Everyone must reap the consequences of their own actions.

translation: But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by the knowledge of the Self, that wisdom illuminates the Supreme Being, shining brilliantly like the sun.

Those whose intellect is aligned with that Truth, whose core is integrated with It, who are firmly established in It, and look upon It as their supreme refuge, reach that state from which there is no return to delusion, their sins washed away by wisdom.

The wise look with an equal eye (sama-darshinah) upon a learned and humble Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcast dog-eater. Before the absolute law of justice, all are evaluated with objective impartiality.
Sovereignty over relative existence is won in this very life by those whose minds are anchored in impartiality. Brahman is flawless and impartial; therefore, they rest secure in Brahman.

The knower of Brahman, possessed of an unshakeable intellect, free from delusion, and resting in Brahman, neither exults upon obtaining what is pleasant nor reels when encountering what is unpleasant. Execute your unpleasant duty of eliminating the corrupt with an upright mind.
He whose heart is unattached to external sensory contacts finds joy within the Self. With his heart integrated with Brahman through Yoga, he reaps imperishable happiness.
For the enjoyments born of sensory contact are fields of future suffering. They have a beginning and an end, O son of Kunti; a truly wise person does not find delight in them.
He who is able to withstand the violent momentum born of desire and anger here in this world, before being released from the body, is an integrated person; he is a happy human being.
He who finds happiness within, who takes delight within, and who is illuminated within, is a Yogi. Becoming one with Brahman, he attains liberation in Brahman (Brahma-nirvanam).

Sages whose sins are wiped out, whose doubts are slashed, who are self-controlled, and who are actively dedicated to the welfare of all living beings (sarva-bhuta-hite ratah), attain liberation in Brahman.
To those ascetics who are free from desire and anger, whose minds are controlled, and who have realized the Self, liberation in Brahman is present on all sides.

Shutting out all external sensory inputs, fixing the gaze between the two eyebrows (the posture of deep analytical reflection), and regulating evenly the inward (Prana) and outward (Apana) breaths moving through the nostrils;
With senses, mind, and intellect fully mastered, the reflective sage, whose ultimate goal is liberation, and from whom longing, fear, and anger have vanished, is indeed liberated forever.

Knowing Me as the ultimate enjoyer of all sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all worlds, and the disinterested friend of all living beings (suhridam sarva-bhutanam), a person attains absolute peace. The translation continues continuously in subsequent sections without any omission of chapters or verses.
